    Welcome to MCERT, the Ministry for Cities, Environment, Regions and Transport. MCERT, has been established to bring together work that shapes the places New Zealanders live, move, build, grow and protect. That includes housing, transport and infrastructure, the environment, regional development and local government. The opportunities and challenges facing New Zealand are increasingly connected. By bringing these areas together, MCERT gives us the chance to take a more joined-up view of place: productive, resilient, well-connected places where people can live well now and into the future. We are building on strong foundations, connecting expertise across systems, and supporting clearer choices and better long-term outcomes for New Zealand. As the way we work becomes more connected, our channels will evolve too. We look forward to continuing to work with our partners and communities as MCERT. http://www.mcert.govt.nz/

    Congratulations to all the winners of the 2025 New Zealand Search and Rescue Awards announced last night!

    New Zealand Search and Rescue (NZSAR)

    1,479 followers

    2w

    Celebrating the 2025 Award winners Congratulations to the winners of the 2025 New Zealand Search and Rescue Awards announced in Wellington last night. Three Gold Awards and seven Certificates of Achievement were presented by Hon James Meager, Associate Minister of Transport, recognising outstanding contributions from teams and individuals across Aotearoa. This year, 52 nominations were received, reflecting the depth of skill, commitment and dedication across the sector. “These Awards reflect not only excellence in individual and team achievement, but also the strength, collaboration and commitment that underpins search and rescue across New Zealand,”said NZSAR Council acting Chair Ruth Fairhall. A special NZSAR Volunteer Service Award was also presented to Surf Life Saving New Zealand, Coastguard Tautīaki Moana, Amateur Radio Emergency Communications (AREC), New Zealand Land Search and Rescue and Fire and Emergency New Zealand – recognising their contribution as part of the United Nations International Volunteer Year (IVY26). Search and rescue relies on thousands of volunteers who give their time, expertise and energy to help others in distress, so more people can come home safely. To see the list of winners and for more information about the Awards please visit https://www.nzsar.govt.nz   Hashtags: #NZSARAwards #searchandrescue

    Protecting our critical underwater infrastructure (CUI): maritime industry partners joined Associate Transport Minister James Meager yesterday for the launch of the National Surveillance and Warning Capability (NSWC) at Kordia’s Maritime Operations Centre (MOC). Based at the MOC, NSWC uses technology that triggers an alert when vessel activity risks damaging nearby CUI. CUI – which includes over 99% of our overseas data travelling through submarine cables and energy between the North and South Island – is at risk of damage by vessels. Even minor contact from fishing gear or anchors can cause damage.   NSWC reduces that risk via a 24/7 monitoring system. The Maritime Security Oversight Committee Secretariat (within the Ministry of Transport) partnered with the Oceania Submarine Cable Association, Starboard Maritime Intelligence, Kordia and Maritime New Zealand to deliver the system. Image credit: Starboard Maritime Intelligence

    The Ministry of Transport is welcoming submissions on proposed regulations to support the modernisation of New Zealand’s road user charges (RUC) system. The regulations are a key part of the Government’s reforms of the RUC system and are needed to ensure any new system is practical, fair and user-friendly. Consultation on the proposed regulations is open until 12 June. The Transport and Infrastructure Select Committee has reported back on the Land Transport (Revenue) Amendment Bill. These regulations support the Bill. To find out more about the consultation and how to make a submission, please visit the consultations page on the MoT website. https://lnkd.in/e9YRAStf

    A new rule extending the restricted licence period for any restricted drivers who receive demerit points comes into force today (7 May). The Government announced changes to the driver licensing system in February making it cheaper and easier for young people to get their driver licence, while at the same time encouraging driver safety. The new system comes into effect on 25 January 2027. Under the new system, drivers will need a clean record while on their restricted licence before they can apply for their full licence. Any restricted driver who receives demerit points from now will have six months added to their restricted period, extending the time before they can apply for their full licence. For more information visit the NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi website. https://lnkd.in/eSiffmJu

    The Ministry of Transport invites submissions on regulations aimed at reducing traffic congestion to support the Land Transport Management (Time of Use Charging) Amendment Act. Traffic congestion in New Zealand’s cities imposes significant costs, including lost time for commuters and freight, unreliable travel times, wasted fuel and higher emissions. From 18 November, local authorities will be able to partner with the New Zealand Transport Agency to propose and establish time of use charging schemes.  The regulations set nationally consistent rules for how time of use charging schemes operate. The consultation is open from Wednesday 29 April to Thursday 25 June. https://lnkd.in/ee9B4erk

    Kiwis are being impacted by increasing global fuel prices and at EECA, we’ve been digging into the role energy efficiency can play right now to support drivers with making savings.   What we've unpacked, is that practical actions – like checking tyre pressure, sitting at a steady speed, and lightening the load – could stretch your tank up to 20%, making every dollar spent on fuel go that much further. Currently this would equate up to a $44 saving on every tank.   While our core focus has been on households, we've also considered macro figures and the numbers are material here too. For example, if just 5% of drivers adopt the actions, weekly fuel use will reduce by up to approximately 1 million litres, equivalent to around $3.5 million in savings each week.   With fuel costs front of mind for many households, we’re encouraging people to give the tips that suit them a go.   Visit our new webpage for more of the detail: https://lnkd.in/eT4DvdQS
